about: Every claim a lesson makes, and where it comes from. A claim's source is either a heading in Docker's docs or a result tested on a real machine. The refresh workflow uses this file to decide whether a docs change affects the course.

sections.heading: A sandbox's rules decide which destinations an agent can reach

claims.text: A request is allowed when any rule allows it, a deny rule from any source overrides an allow rule, and a request no rule decides is blocked by the fallback.
Under the Balanced preset, a request that matches no rule is blocked and the sandbox asks for approval.
A destination is a host and a port. pypi.org:443 is allowed and pypi.org:80 is denied.
A deny rule for api.github.com blocks it even though a group allows **.github.com.

sections.heading: A preset and a kit supply the rules a sandbox starts with

claims.text: There are three presets: Open, Balanced, and Locked Down. The preset is chosen the first time you run a sandbox and applies to every sandbox on the machine.
A machine on the Balanced preset with one Claude Code sandbox lists three policies: local-policy, default-deny-all, and a kit policy.
The fallback blocks any request no other rule decides, and it never overrides an allow rule.
A kit brings its own allow rules. They apply only to sandboxes that use the kit, and they can't be edited.
The Balanced preset holds 195 network allow rules in six rule IDs, and the Claude Code kit policy holds eight.
Policies can also hold filesystem rules, which control the host folders a sandbox can mount.

sections.heading: Every rule you add or remove changes what the team can do

claims.text: Removing a rule group blocks every destination that only that group allowed.
Allowing a host makes that one destination reachable again.
Denying a host blocks that destination, even when a group or a kit allows it.
The kit policy stays in place whatever you remove from the local policy. With default-ai-services removed, api.anthropic.com is still allowed in a sandbox that uses the Claude Code kit.
The Cloud infrastructure group also contains cdn.playwright.dev and other hosts that aren't cloud providers.

sections.heading: A wildcard allows more than it names

claims.text: A one-star wildcard matches exactly one subdomain level and doesn't match the bare domain.
A two-star wildcard matches subdomains at any depth.
A two-star wildcard also matches the bare domain: **.amazonaws.com allows amazonaws.com.

sections.heading: The CLI documents itself, so ask it before you guess

claims.text: The help output for sbx policy and sbx policy rm network, as shown.

sections.heading: Listing the policies shows you who set each rule

claims.text: sbx policy ls shows one row for each policy, with its source, what it applies to, and a summary.
sbx policy ls SANDBOX shows the combined policy for one sandbox.

source.heading: List the policies for one sandbox

claims.text: The listing output, as shown.

sections.heading: Inspecting a group shows everything you're about to remove

claims.text: sbx policy inspect shows a policy's rules or one rule's details.
The inspect output for local-policy and default-cloud-infrastructure, as shown.

sections.heading: Each change takes effect at once, so check after each one

claims.text: sbx policy check network reports whether a destination is allowed, and names the deciding rule or reason.

source.heading: Check whether a destination is allowed

claims.text: sbx policy allow network and sbx policy deny network add a rule for a host.
sbx policy rm network removes a rule by ID or by resource, after a confirmation prompt.
Every command output in this section, as shown.

sections.heading: A command can succeed and still do the wrong thing

claims.text: sbx policy deny network with a rule ID in place of a host adds a deny rule for a host of that name and leaves the group in place.
Allowing a host that's already covered prints 'Already covered' and changes nothing.

sections.heading: Prove the policy matches your decision

claims.text: A denied check exits with status 1, so the command can be used in a script.

source.heading: Check whether a destination is allowed

claims.text: sbx policy reset deletes every local rule, stops running sandboxes, and asks for a preset.
